title: Livingstone across Africa
vehicle: On foot and by canoe, with Makololo companions
summary: The Scottish missionary sets out from the Makololo capital Linyanti to find a route to the coast: west to Luanda on the Atlantic, back again, then east down the Zambezi past the falls he named Victoria to Quelimane on the Indian Ocean. The first documented crossing of southern Africa by a European, told in his bestseller "Missionary Travels".

sources.label: History Today: Livingstone reaches the Victoria Falls

approximate: Main places and dates from his account; dates differ slightly between sources, and the straight lines are a rough guide.

stops.name: Linyanti
stops.text: The Makololo capital by the Chobe, where chief Sekeletu gave him men for the journey.

stops.name: Lake Dilolo
stops.text: Up the Zambezi and across the watershed between the Zambezi and the Congo.

stops.name: Cassange
stops.text: The Portuguese trading post on the Kwango, after months of fever.

stops.name: Luanda
stops.text: The Atlantic. He refused a passage home, to take his companions back as promised.

stops.name: Back at Linyanti
stops.text: More than a year to walk back, retracing the route.

stops.name: Victoria Falls
stops.text: "Mosi-oa-Tunya", the smoke that thunders: he named it for his queen.

stops.name: Kafue confluence
stops.text: Across the plateau and down to where the Kafue joins the Zambezi.

stops.name: Zumbo
stops.text: The ruins of an old Portuguese post at the Luangwa confluence.

stops.name: Tete
stops.text: Cutting across a loop of the river, he missed the Cahora Bassa rapids, a mistake that later cost him dearly.

stops.name: Quelimane
stops.text: The Indian Ocean, two and a half years after leaving Linyanti.
